name: fused

obs_groups.title: Where it thinks it is
obs_groups.note: the navigation filter's answer - this is where the towers and satellites actually enter

obs_groups.title: What it just did
obs_groups.note: its own last command, so it can be smooth

obs_sources: Flight-plan waypoint minus the navigation filter's position estimate (IMU + ground towers + Iridium Doppler), rotated into the aeroplane's own frame. Any error in the fix is an error in this number. Distance along the current ground track, scaled by 10 km.

Flight-plan waypoint minus the navigation filter's position estimate (IMU + ground towers + Iridium Doppler), rotated into the aeroplane's own frame. Any error in the fix is an error in this number. Distance across the track, positive to the right.

Flight-plan waypoint minus the navigation filter's position estimate (IMU + ground towers + Iridium Doppler), rotated into the aeroplane's own frame. Any error in the fix is an error in this number. Height difference to the waypoint.

Flight-plan waypoint minus the navigation filter's position estimate (IMU + ground towers + Iridium Doppler), rotated into the aeroplane's own frame. Any error in the fix is an error in this number. The waypoint AFTER this one, so a turn can be started early.

Flight-plan waypoint minus the navigation filter's position estimate (IMU + ground towers + Iridium Doppler), rotated into the aeroplane's own frame. Any error in the fix is an error in this number. Across-track distance to the next-but-one waypoint.

Flight-plan waypoint minus the navigation filter's position estimate (IMU + ground towers + Iridium Doppler), rotated into the aeroplane's own frame. Any error in the fix is an error in this number. Height difference to the next-but-one waypoint.
Horizontal speed over the ground, from the navigation filter's velocity estimate. It differs from airspeed by the wind, which is never given to the agent directly.
Climb or descent rate, from the navigation filter's velocity estimate.
Pitot tube: speed through the air, with about 1.5 m/s of noise. A direct sensor - no filter involved.
AHRS roll angle, with 0.4 deg of noise and a fixed bias drawn per flight. Scaled by the 45 deg bank limit.
AHRS pitch (flight path angle), same errors, scaled by the 8 deg limit.
Accelerometer, ECEF x axis: a constant bias plus white noise. This is the signal whose bias makes dead reckoning run away.
Altitude from the navigation filter's position estimate (IMU + ground towers + Iridium Doppler), minus the 9,000 m target. Wrong by however wrong the fix is.
Its own bank command from the previous tick - the reward penalises thrashing.
Its own pitch command from the previous tick.
Its own throttle setting from the previous tick.
The filter's own position uncertainty (log10 of 1 sigma, over 3). It rises when towers drop out of range and falls when the geometry is good.
